topic: Your first twenty bowls are supposed to collapse

slides.headline: Your first twenty bowls are supposed to **collapse**.
Most beginners quit in week two.
slides.body:
They center the clay, pull a wall, and watch it fold.

Then they decide they have no talent for it.

slides.headline: A flop is the clay showing you **where it went thin**.
Cut it in half
slides.body: Take a wire and slice the flop from rim to base. The wall shows you the exact spot it gave out.

slides.headline: Wedge it and go again
slides.body: Same clay, same night. Your hands remember more from the second pull than from any video.

slides.headline: I kept count my first year.
slides.body: **61 flops** before one bowl reached the kiln. That bowl still holds my keys.

slides.headline: Want the six-week beginner plan?
slides.body: Comment the word below and I will send it to you.

caption:
Every new class goes quiet around minute forty.

That is when the first walls come down, and I can see who is about to decide they are bad at this.

So I started a ritual. We line the flops up on the wedging table and I cut mine open first.

Comment WEDGE and I will send you the plan I hand every beginner on night one.
